title: Forms of Business Organisation
lines: USAT-COM questions on business organisation test whether you can tell the forms apart: who owns, who controls, how far the owners are liable, and which document governs the business. Expect questions on kinds of partners, company documents, kinds of shares and capital, cooperative principles and types of public enterprise. Most wrong options are true of a different form of business, so compare the forms side by side.
## Sole proprietorship

One person supplies the capital, manages, takes all the profit and bears all the loss. It is easy to start, decisions are quick, the owner keeps personal contact with customers and business secrets stay private.
- Liability is unlimited: the owner's private property can be taken to pay business debts.
- Capital and managing ability are limited to one person.
- The business has no separate legal existence; it may end with the owner's death or illness.
## Partnership

In Pakistan partnerships are governed by the Partnership Act, 1932. A partnership is the relation between persons who agree to share the profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all. So at least two persons are needed, and each partner is an agent of the firm and of the others (mutual agency).
- The partnership deed records capital, profit-sharing ratio, salaries, interest and duties.
- If the deed is silent, profits and losses are shared equally.
- Liability is unlimited and joint and several: a creditor can recover the whole debt from any partner.
- Registration is optional, but an unregistered firm cannot sue outsiders to enforce its contracts.
- A new partner can be admitted only with the consent of all partners.
| Kind of partner | Capital | Manages | Known to public
| active (working) | yes | yes | yes
| sleeping (dormant) | yes | no | usually not
| nominal | no | no | yes, lends his name
| secret | yes | yes | no

A minor cannot be a full partner, but with all partners' consent he can be admitted to the benefits of partnership; his liability is limited to his share in the firm. A partnership at will has no fixed period and can be dissolved by notice. Dissolution is compulsory when all, or all but one, partners become insolvent or the business becomes unlawful.
## Joint stock company

A company is an artificial person created by registration under the companies law; in Pakistan, the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) registers and regulates companies. Its features:
- separate legal entity: it owns property, sues and is sued in its own name;
- perpetual succession: members may change or die, the company continues;
- limited liability: a shareholder can lose at most the unpaid amount on his shares;
- management by elected directors, not by all members;
- transferable shares in a public company.
A private company restricts the transfer of its shares and cannot invite the public to buy them; a public company can, through a prospectus.
## Company documents and doctrines
| Document | Purpose
| memorandum of association | charter: name, registered office, objects, liability, capital; relations with outsiders
| articles of association | internal rules: meetings, directors, voting, transfer of shares
| certificate of incorporation | the company is born on its date
| prospectus | invites the public to buy shares or debentures
- Ultra vires: an act beyond the objects in the memorandum is void and cannot be ratified even by all members.
- Constructive notice: outsiders are presumed to know the memorandum and articles.
- Indoor management: outsiders acting in good faith may assume internal procedures were followed.
## Shares, debentures and capital
- Ordinary shareholders own the company, vote, and receive a dividend that varies with profit.
- Preference shareholders receive a fixed dividend before ordinary shareholders and are repaid capital first on winding up. Cumulative preference dividends unpaid in a bad year are carried forward.
- Debenture holders are creditors who receive fixed interest whether or not there is a profit.
- Bonus shares are free, issued from reserves. Right shares are offered first to existing members and paid for.
Capital: authorised (maximum in the memorandum) → issued → subscribed → called-up → paid-up (called-up less calls in arrears). Reserve capital can be called only on winding up.
An ordinary resolution needs a simple majority; a special resolution needs at least three-fourths of the votes cast.
## Cooperatives and public enterprises

A cooperative society is a voluntary association for mutual service. Principles: open membership, one member one vote, democratic management by an elected committee, limited return on capital, and surplus shared by patronage. Types include consumers', producers', credit, marketing and housing societies.

Public enterprises are owned by the state: a departmental undertaking is run by a ministry and financed by the budget; a statutory (public) corporation is created by a special Act and is a separate legal person; a government company is registered under the companies law with the state holding a majority of shares.
## Worked examples
> A company issues 50,000 shares of Rs. 10, calls Rs. 7, and Rs. 3 is unpaid on 2,000 shares.
> Called-up = 50,000 × 7 = Rs. 350,000. Calls in arrears = 2,000 × 3 = Rs. 6,000.
> Paid-up = Rs. 344,000.
> Asad invests in a firm but never visits the office.
> He is a sleeping partner and still has unlimited liability for the firm's debts.
## Traps
! Sharing profits in the capital ratio applies only if agreed; the default is equal sharing.
! Mutual agency is a feature of partnership, not of a company.
! A debenture holder is a creditor, not an owner.
! "One share, one vote" is the company rule; cooperatives use one member, one vote.
## Quick check
- Which document governs a company's internal management? (articles of association)
- Which partner lends only his name? (nominal partner)
- What majority does a special resolution need? (three-fourths of votes cast)
- Which public enterprise is created by its own Act? (statutory corporation)
